description: Lockfiles with known vulnerable dependencies (plan 2B): 4 Trivy findings, against the Trivy database pinned in tools/analyzers/install.sh

notes.database: captured with Trivy 0.74.0 and the database snapshot pinned in tools/analyzers/install.sh (TRIVY_DB_DIGEST sha256:7d0ae3ee…, built 2026-09-25T06:36:11Z), offline (docker run --network none), with the adapter's own flags (config.md §6); the raw output is cli/test/analyzer-output/trivy-deps-vulnerable.json, over a byte-for-byte copy of these lockfiles. A newer database can know more vulnerabilities of these versions: the packages were chosen for stable, years-old advisories (minimist 1.2.5 has one, commons-collections 3.2.1 two), but moving the pin (pnpm trivy-db:pin) must re-run this fixture and update it when the database learned something new
notes.web/package-lock.json:15: npm lockfile v3: Trivy places minimist 1.2.5 at its entry "node_modules/minimist", lines 14-19; the CLI locates it at the entry's "version": "1.2.5" line, 15, so an upgrade that changes the version is new code (ruling T3)
notes.tools/pnpm-lock.yaml:17: pnpm lockfile v9: Trivy gives no position, so the CLI takes the first line holding minimist@1.2.5 as a whole word, the packages entry at line 17 (the snapshots entry at line 22 comes later)
notes.java/gradle.lockfile:4: Gradle lockfile: Trivy places commons-collections 3.2.1 at line 4, which holds its version; junit 4.12 (CVE-2020-15250) and hamcrest are test-only configurations, development dependencies Trivy leaves out
notes.files: package.json, lockfiles and manifests are files of language other (config.md §3.1 includes them); each line count is the file's own (wc -l)
